dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin.
Yes, good evening. Um, I know it's past five, City Hall's closed and all, but the recording said this line was still picking up for the storm business. Is that right?
Yep, you got the right place. We keep this line open after hours for storm stuff. What's going on?
Well, it's the low spot at the end of my block. On Kingston Avenue. I'm at 451. And the water down there is sitting, oh, about a foot deep, I'd say. Maybe a little more by the curb.
A foot. Okay, and that's from the nor'easter?

Yes, from last weekend's storm, Saturday into Sunday. It's Monday now and it hasn't gone down hardly at all. I walked down this afternoon to look, and I don't like it. It was not this bad last winter, I can tell you that. We had puddles, sure, but nothing like this.

Got it. So 451 Kingston, low spot at the end of the block, about a foot of standing water, still there a day after the storm. I'm writing that down. Is it up on anyone's property, or is it just in the street?

Just in the street, mostly. It's creeping up toward the sidewalk on the one side. No houses taking it yet that I can see, but I worry, you know, if it rains again. The drain there, I can't even see the grate, it's all under.
Yeah, that'll do it. Can you get a car through there, or is it blocked off?

Well, nobody's driving through it. A fella in a pickup tried it earlier and then thought better. Oh, and the new neighbors, they just moved in across from the corner, they came out to look too. They've got a flag on the porch, a blue and, hmm, yellow and white one, and I couldn't tell you what it is. Anyway, they were standing there shaking their heads same as me.
Okay. Well, I'll note the neighbors are watching it too. Anything else you can see, like debris or leaves packed around the grate?

Hard to say with the water over it. There's some sticks floating. Say, can I ask you something? When did they last come by down there? To clean it out, I mean. I can't remember seeing a truck in a long while.

That I can't tell you off the top of my head. I don't have the cleaning schedule in front of me on this screen. I'll put the question in the ticket so the crew supervisor can answer it, and I'll mark it as standing water, ongoing.
I'd appreciate that. I'm seventy-some years old and I'm not out there with a boot and a stick, but I do worry about it freezing over tonight. It's supposed to get cold.
Good point, I'll flag the freezing too. Ice on top of a foot of water is a real problem on a street. Do you want a call back with an answer on the last cleaning?
Yes, please. The number is four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-nine-eight.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-nine-eight. And it's Mr. Lopes, right? L-O-P-E-S?
That's right. Joel Lopes.

Okay, Joel, you're all set. The ticket goes to the day crew in the morning, and somebody should call you back once they've looked at it. If it gets worse tonight, like water heading toward a house, call this line again.
I will. Thank you, Kevin. I'm glad somebody picks up this late.
No problem. Stay dry, Joel.
